A Canary fingerprint is checked at most once a day and replaced automatically once it is within about two weeks of expiring. Canary configs expire roughly 6 weeks from their release date — the expiry is shown in the active config summary.

For manual setup:
1. Tap "Fetch Pixel Canary fingerprint" and select a device.
2. If no devices are found, import a working PIF config from a trusted source. Config files are not provided.
3. Recheck your Play Integrity status.

Always delete the active configuration before importing a new one. Loading an expired PIF config will cause TrickyStore strong integrity to fail even with a valid keybox.

Advanced spoofing:
• Play Store fingerprint spoof — leave disabled unless advised otherwise. Spoofing FINGERPRINT to Play Store is rarely needed and may cause issues.
• Spoof SDK to Play Store — presents SDK 32 to the Play Store to force the legacy pre-Android 13 verdict path. It can break Play Store behavior, so leave it off unless testing.
• Spoof build fields and system properties — leave on. They present the fingerprint to DroidGuard.
• Spoof keystore provider — keep off when a keybox is in use, since it bypasses keybox attestation.
• Spoof ROM signature — experimental.

A keybox is fetched and kept valid automatically. The revocation status is checked every 24 hours, and a new keybox is fetched from the official source if the current one is revoked or suspended.

For manual setup:
1. Tap "Fetch latest keybox" to download one automatically, or import your own from a trusted source.
2. Open "Manage target apps" and select the apps that require integrity checks.
3. Set target mode to "Leaf" if your device has a working TEE; otherwise leave it as Auto.
4. Recheck your Play Integrity status.

Note: If no valid latest keybox is available, auto-fetch is paused for 24 hours before retrying. Always delete the existing keybox before importing a new one.
